newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinaoil seeks bigger slice of oil import trade.
newsitem.headline: Chinaoil seeks bigger slice of oil import trade.

text.p: Chinese state oil trader Chinaoil said on Friday it aimed to gain a bigger slice of the nation's oil import trade.
"We aim to get a bigger share of oil import trade in China," said Lin Qingshan, Chinaoil president told Reuters in an interview.

Chinaoil, set up in 1993 as a joint venture between state oil trader Sinochem and onshore oil producer China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC), imported about 1.8 million tonnes of oil products in 1996, up about 50 percent over the previous year, Lin said.
Lin said he expected China to import over 10 million tonnes of oil products this year. He expects fuel oil to dominate imports, citing strong demand from China's power industry.
Imports of refined oil products are currently split among China's three state traders, Sinochem, Chinaoil and Unipec.
Chinaoil also exports crude oil but China's growing domestic demand for crude oil is likely to cut into the amount available for export.
